description: The article operationalizes maintained situational interest not by verbal self-report but behaviorally: participants decided which of six described seminar topics (Experiment 1) or which of six take-home texts (Experiment 2) they wanted to engage with, and the count of yes-responses was the measure.
title: Behavioral choice measure of maintained situational interest

description: A real-time observational coding protocol in which coders watch video of small groups without a transcript and note the exact time of changes in vocal register, affect, grammar, gesture production, and body language.
title: Behavioral coding methodology for identifying epistemological framing in group video

description: The chapter holds that telemetry \"should have the following properties: (a) is a description of behavior and not an inference about why behavior occurs, (b) is unambiguous,\" and (c) contains sufficient context to link the element to a specific player at a specific point.
title: Behavioral telemetry logging with observable, unambiguous, contextualized events

description: The article outlines a benefit-cost analysis framework for SEL interventions in which costs and benefits are compared in monetary values to derive a net present value.
title: Benefit-cost analysis framework for SEL interventions

description: A BERT-based model the authors train to learn embeddings for math strategies from MATHia student log data, together with a prediction task that distinguishes between successful and unsuccessful strategy use.
title: BERT strategy-embedding and successful-strategy prediction from MATHia logs

description: A six-step NLP pipeline the authors applied to 11,540 NMLE item texts (stems plus answer choices): preprocessing with the MeCab morphological analyzer and the MANBYO medical dictionary, embedding with the Japanese Sentence Transformer model \"sonoisa/sentence-bert-base-ja-mean-tokens-v2\", UMAP dimens
title: BERTopic-based topic modeling pipeline for educational assessment corpora

description: The between-student method, first used in physics by Sayre and Heckler, gives short conceptual quizzes to different sub-groups of the population in successive weeks, avoiding test-retest effects.
title: Between-student testing and response-curve method
